13956.etyen:
Univerbation of far (“to fare, travel”) + vel (“well”), literally “fare well”. The expression continues Old Norse far vel (“farewell”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *far wela (“farewell”). The Proto-Germanic expression consists of *faraną (“to go, travel”), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“to go through; carry forth, fare”), and *wela (“well”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- (“to choose, want”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk farvel, Danish farvel, Swedish farväl, Icelandic farvel, Dutch vaarwel, German Fahrwohl and English farewell.

1000836.etyen:
From nord (“north”) + Aurdal (“place name”), literally “northern Aurdal”. The official name was changed from Nordre Aurdal to Nord-Aurdal in 1917. Aurdal probably contains the lost river name Aura, interpreted as “the gravel river”, ultimately related to aurr (“gravel; wet clay, mud”), with dalr (“valley”) as the final element.
Compare the parallel formation Sør-Aurdal (“southern Aurdal”).

1001092.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Latin Hispaniola, a Latinized rendering used by Peter Martyr d'Anghiera for Spanish La Española, shortened from la Isla Española (“the Spanish island”), the name given to the island by Christopher Columbus in 1492.
Spanish española (“Spanish”) is the feminine singular of español (“Spanish”), agreeing with isla (“island”). The Latinized form is formally analyzable as Hispania + -ola, from Hispania (“Spain; the Iberian Peninsula”) and the diminutive suffix -ola; however, the underlying Spanish name means “the Spanish island”, not “little Spain”.
